help.workflowBody: Open or drop an audio file. Set BPM and grid, then add markers to split the waveform. Name and export slices in Output. Save your work as a .wosdx project. Use Relink audio after moving the audio file.
help.workspaceBody: Click or drag the track’s waveform overview to move along the timeline. New panels open at the right edge and move older panels left. Click a panel’s switch again or its close button to hide it. Panels can fill the workspace. If space is insufficient, the oldest panel closes. There is no horizontal scrollbar, and closed panels keep your input. Project → Add audio track adds a track with its own audio and markers. Click a track to edit it; double-click its name to rename it. Playback plays all tracks; use M and S on a track to mute or solo it.
help.mouseBody: Left-drag adds markers. Right-drag removes them. Drag a marker to move the selected markers. Shift-drag adds to the selection, and Ctrl/Cmd-drag toggles selection within a range. Middle-drag pans, Ctrl/Cmd+wheel zooms, and Alt temporarily disables snapping. Press {cancel} to cancel a drag.
help.keyboardScope: Shortcuts work in the editor, outside text fields and dialogs. Ctrl/Cmd means Ctrl on Windows/Linux or Command on macOS. Buttons, sliders and tabs use standard keyboard navigation.
help.calibrationBody: Load audio and open Tools → Calibrate. Tap {keys} with the clicks. When the median stabilizes, select Finish, then Apply. Press {cancel} to close. The offset corrects marker timing during playback.
help.placeBreakpoint: Add marker at playhead or cursor
help.shiftAllMinus: Move all markers back one tick
help.shiftAllPlus: Move all markers forward one tick
help.audioFormats: WAV, AIFF, FLAC, Ogg Vorbis, MP3, AAC-LC and ALAC; mono or stereo. Processing uses Float32; WAV export uses 16-bit PCM. AAC may include encoder delay or padding. MKV/MKA accepts these codecs, excluding Opus. MKV/MKA decodes one audio track; an implicit default flag can cause selection of the first track. Extract the desired track first if needed.

input.altNavigation: Press and release Alt to focus the menu bar. Press a marked letter to open its menu, or use Alt+letter. Arrow keys move, Enter selects, Esc returns, and Alt exits. Menu letters are the same in all languages.
input.gamepadScope: Focus this window. A adds a marker, X toggles the marker at the cursor, Y previews and RT plays. The left stick or D-pad moves the cursor; the right stick zooms and moves by ticks. LB and RB move by measures. Hold a direction to repeat. Use the buttons above to switch between keyboard and controller controls.
input.dialogNavigation: These buttons are fixed. In menus and dialogs, the D-pad or left stick selects, A activates and B goes back. LT and RT scroll the help and troubleshooting pages.
input.wheelGamepad: Hold LT, point a stick or the D-pad at a command and release LT to run it. Release without pointing to cancel, or press B. Tap LT to keep the wheel open, then point and press A. LB and RB switch wheels.
input.wheelKeyboard: Hold {key}, move the mouse toward a command and release {key} to run it. Release at the center or press Esc to cancel. Tap {key} to keep the wheel open, then click a command. Scroll to switch wheels.

support.intro: Copy diagnostics when reporting a problem. They include build, display and controller details. Audio, project contents and file paths are excluded. Nothing is sent automatically.
support.audioBody: Check the system output device, playback volume and cue volume. For missing audio, select the original file in Project → Relink audio. Reopen audio after a decoding failure.
support.gamepadBody: Connect the Xbox controller, focus this window, then press a button. Select Refresh diagnostics to check the controller list. Menu opens menus, and View opens the guide. Switch control references manually with the guide buttons. Leave text fields and dialogs before editing. If the controller is missing, check its system connection and reconnect it.
support.recoveryDesktop: Save your project before restarting. If recovery keeps failing, exit the app. Move session-v2.json from the recovery data folder to another location as a backup. Restart and open a saved project. Keep the original audio and project files.
support.recoveryWeb: Save your project before reloading. You may need to relink audio after recovery. If recovery keeps failing, back up your project. Follow the site data cleanup steps below. This deletes recovery data and settings.
support.backupFirst: Save projects you want to keep. Cleanup deletes recovery data and settings, including unsaved work.
support.desktopLocate: Before exiting, note all data folders in Help → Troubleshoot. Windows uses both Roaming and Local folders. Help → Open data folder opens the recovery data folder.
support.desktopRemove: Close all woslicer-dx windows. Uninstall installed copies through the operating system. For portable copies, delete the extracted app folder.
support.desktopData: After exiting, delete the listed app data folders. This removes recovery data, file permissions, window settings, WebView storage and cache.
support.webClose: Close this site’s tabs and installed web app windows. Remove any web app or shortcut you created. Select the data removal option if available.
support.webData: Find this site in browser settings under cookies, site data or site permissions. Delete all its data, including cookies, local storage and databases. Select only this site. Keep other sites’ data.
support.webCache: To remove downloaded page files, delete cached images and files in the browser’s browsing data settings. This may clear the cache for the whole browser profile. Do not select unrelated data.
support.personalFiles: Downloaded projects, exported audio and original files are separate. Keep files you need and delete others manually.

recording.modeHint: Record taps as markers while listening
recording.description: Enable Record in the playback bar to record each tap as a marker at the playhead. Seeking moves by {seconds} seconds and keeps playback paused or playing. Markers follow the snap and tap-offset settings.
recording.stickHint: Rotate LS around its edge: clockwise seeks forward, counterclockwise seeks backward. Each eighth turn moves one step. Holding a direction does not seek. LT, the right stick, Menu and View keep their editing functions.
recording.yuanconHint: Connect through Tools → YuanCon controller. The seven keys place markers. Forward rotation toggles playback once; reverse rotation keeps seeking backward while active. Use the keyboard or mouse for menus.
recording.yuanconDescription: Connect a YuanCon seven-key controller with a turntable to record markers.
recording.unavailable: Device access is unavailable here. Open the web app in desktop Chrome or Edge.
recording.directionHint: Turn the platter forward. If Reverse appears, enable Reverse turntable direction.
recording.previewHint: This dialog displays input only. Each key lights up separately; check that numbers 1–7 match the physical keys from left to right.
recording.unsupportedReport: This controller mode is unsupported. Check the device mode and reconnect.
recording.keysHint: Markers store key numbers 1–7, including chords. Keys at the same marker are merged. Save as .wosdx to keep key numbers; .wos does not store them.
